conviction_note: Findings on their own sum to about +0.05: the strongest item, a counterparty read from HD, points to a Q3 comp above Lowe's ~flat guide, and an EPS bar pinned to the guide leaves room for an unguided tariff-refund upside. Against that, LOW ran ~8 pts ahead of XHB over 20 days into the print, HD's own beat was sold (-1.8% intraday), and the FY27 framework is held back to the 9 Dec investor day. The scaled number, p_up 53 x 3.8% abs move = +0.23, leans slightly up because LOW has bought its last two prints, including a guide cut to the low end. The two measurements agree in sign and are both small.

The EPS and revenue bars are therefore sourced to the guide and to three agreeing estimates. The comp bar is weaker: the company guided Q3 comps 'in line with the FY', i.e. ~flat; one aggregator snippet says the street expects ~+0.4%, but no primary estimate source was found. HD's quarter ran ahead of its plan and HD said November is tracking its guide. FY27 targets are held for the 2026-12-09 investor conference. The most likely outcome is a maintained FY guide with comps nudged toward the top of 'flat' or EPS lifted only by refunds; a cut looks unlikely given HD's read.

findings.finding: Counterparty read: Home Depot's Q3 (to 2026-11-01) US comps were +2.2% against a street ~1.5%. That accelerated from +1.3% US in Q2, when Lowe's comped +0.2%, a 1.1-point gap. Monthly US comps were Aug +1.1%, Sep +4.4%, Oct +1.3%. Big-ticket (>$1,000) was +4.5%, led by appliances and power, and HD said it was 'less promotional than prior years'. If the Q2 HD-LOW gap simply holds, LOW's Q3 comp lands near +1% against a company guide of ~flat and a loosely sourced street ~+0.4%.
findings.link: Direct duopoly competitor. Same quarter (HD to Nov 1, LOW to ~Oct 31), same categories (appliances are LOW's largest big-ticket line), same DIY/Pro customers. HD and LOW together hold ~a quarter of the TAM (Ellison, 2026-09-15). LOW blamed its July softness on a competitor's tariff-refund-funded promotions, which HD now says it pulled back from.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Comps are LOW's swing line. Q3 FY25 comps +0.4% missed a 1.3% expectation and the stock still rose +4.03% on an EPS beat. Q2 FY26 comps +0.2% with a guide cut: +2.02%.
findings.why_not_priced: HD printed this morning, and the LOW consensus ($2.86, comps ~flat to +0.4%) was set against LOW's own August guide before it. If the market had moved LOW's comp bar up to HD's pace, LOW would have traded with HD's beat today; instead it fell ~1% alongside HD (-1.8%), which treats HD's day as a margin/guide story, not a demand read. One limit applies: LOW's transactions (-2.1% in Q2) have lagged HD's (-1.0%), so the gap could widen rather than hold.
findings.independence: Monthly comps and promotion come from the HD Q3 call transcript, the same company (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-home-depot-tops-q3-2026-estimates-shares-slip-93CH-5033430). Placer.ai visit data (separate finding) is an independent series pointing the same way. The comp bar is loosely sourced, so this finding is capped.

findings.finding: Placer.ai foot traffic: Lowe's same-store visits were -0.4% YoY in September and -0.8% in October. HD stayed within ±0.5 pt of last year in each Q3 month and was -1.0% in October. LOW's traffic ran roughly level with HD's while HD turned flat traffic plus +3% ticket into a +2.2% comp.
findings.why_not_priced: Traffic data published 6 days before the print says the two chains were roughly level on visits. That makes HD's comp transferable to LOW unless LOW's ticket lags. Nothing in LOW's estimate drift (lower over 60 days) reflects it. This is a proxy: visits are not sales, and LOW's ticket growth (+2.3% in Q2) has run below HD's (+2.8%).
findings.independence: Independent of the HD documents. Points the same way as the HD counterparty finding.

findings.finding: Price path into the print: LOW is +12.2% over 20 sessions against XHB +4.0%, and +18% since 10-14 against XHB +7.8%. Stifel calls the run +27.6% since early October. That is a sector housing/midterm rally (2026-11-04) on which LOW outran the ETF by ~8 pts, then gave back -3.9% in the last 5 sessions against XHB -3.0%. With spot ~12% below the mean target, a clean in-line print may not hold LOW's premium to the sector.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: LOW bought its last two prints (+2.02%, +4.03%) even on comp misses and a guide cut, so this name has not been selling beats. Across 7 prints: 5 up, median |move| 1.93%.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up itself is visible to everyone. The point is that the rally was macro and election-driven, not a change in LOW's numbers: estimates drifted lower over the same 60 days (Investing.com), so the price now expects more than the consensus does. The 5-day giveback shows part of this has already been taken out, so the finding is sized well below the ~8-point outperformance.
findings.independence: XHB chart (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/XHB?range=2mo&interval=1d); midterm housing rally (https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/housing-stocks-rally-following-midterm-elections-treasury-yields-dip-lower-171937967.html, 2026-11-04); Stifel's +27.6% (https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/lowes-earnings-loom-as-diy-weakness-tests-home-improvement-outlook-93CH-4988214). HD's reaction today is kept as a separate finding because it is a different fact (a peer reaction function, not a price level).

findings.finding: Peer reaction function: HD beat on comps (+2.2% vs ~1.5%) and revenue ($43.4B vs $42.7-42.8B), but EPS was only in line ($3.86 vs $3.84-3.86) and the margin and EPS guide narrowed to ~+2% from 0-4%. The stock traded -1.8% intraday on 2026-11-17 ($347.51 to $341.27).
findings.link: Same sector, same quarter, the closest comparable. Investors read the two names as a pair (HD ~23x forward, LOW ~17-18x).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: LOW's own beats were bought on the last two prints. HD's sell-off is a peer data point, not LOW's history.
findings.why_not_priced: It is partly priced: LOW traded down with HD today. It still sets a precedent that a demand beat without margin or guide improvement gets sold, and LOW's margins are also under pressure (Q2 adj op margin -62 bp, FBM/ADG dilutive). An intraday HD move is not a close.
findings.independence: HD intraday price from Yahoo chart (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/HD?range=1mo&interval=1d); the Investing.com transcript headline 'shares slip'. Shares HD documents with the counterparty finding, but a different fact (the reaction, not the comp).

findings.finding: Tariff refunds sit outside the guide. Q2 adjusted EPS included an $80M / $0.11 IEEPA refund. The FY guide excludes further H2 refunds, and the CFO said 'we are moving through the filing process for additional refunds'. BofA estimates refunds could add ~$0.53/share; HD received ~$685-730M. Any Q3 recognition would sit on top of an EPS bar ($2.86) that equals the ex-refund guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26: an EPS beat that included $0.11 of refunds, with revenue missing and the guide cut, bought +2.02%. The refund was not what the stock traded on.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS ($2.86-2.89) sits on the guide's ~-7%, which excludes refunds, so a recognised refund would print as an adjusted EPS beat. Analysts usually exclude refunds from forward models, and a class action (filed September) claims shoppers are owed them, so even a large refund would add only a fraction of its face value to the multiple. Its path into the FY EPS guide (above $12.25) is possible but one-off.
findings.independence: BofA estimate via https://finimize.com/content/bofa-sees-lowes-2026-outlook-looking-more-predictable (undated, pre-print). Class action: https://www.claimdepot.com/cases/lowes-class-action-alleges-retailer-kept-tariff-refunds-consumers-helped-fund.

findings.finding: Inside the quarter, at the Goldman Sachs conference on 2026-09-15, Ellison said H2 will look 'a lot like the first half' (H1 comps +0.6% and +0.2%), pricing about the same and not 'overly promotional'. He called Q2 the most promotional period in 25 years, tied it to tariff refunds and said 'we believe it's transitory'. Profit-algorithm detail is deferred to the December investor conference. No pre-release or 8-K reaffirmation was found.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior mid-quarter statement reaction on file.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and broadly priced. It shows management was not flagging a deterioration six weeks into the quarter. HD's comment that promotion eased is consistent with Ellison's 'transitory'.
findings.independence: HD call: 'less promotional than prior years' (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-home-depot-tops-q3-2026-estimates-shares-slip-93CH-5033430).

findings.finding: Next guide: the FY26 guide (comps ~flat, adj EPS ~$12.25, ex-refunds) is most likely maintained, with the possibility of a refund-driven EPS lift or comps toward the top of 'flat'. A cut is unlikely: HD's Q3 ran ahead of its plan and HD said November is tracking its guide. FY27 targets are held for the 2026-12-09 investor conference, so the release carries no new-year guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26: guide cut to the low end, stock +2.02%. Q1 FY26 (2026-05-20): guide maintained, +1.23%. Q4 FY25 (2026-02-25), which carried the first FY26 guide: -5.59%, the largest move in the history.
findings.why_not_priced: The street's EPS sits on the guide. An implied negative Q4 comp (~-0.5% to -1%) leaves room to keep the FY comp guide at 'flat' even with a ~+1% Q3. The market has not been given anything above the guide since August.
findings.independence: HD: 'first few weeks of November are consistent with that guidance' (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-home-depot-tops-q3-2026-estimates-shares-slip-93CH-5033430). Investor-day date: https://www.benzinga.com/quote/LOW/events.

findings.finding: Analyst actions into the print: Stifel cut LOW to Sell, target $190 from $195 (2026-11-13), citing weaker H2 housing, FY27-28 margin pressure and the FBM/ADG specialty platform's exposure to new construction. Zelman also moved to Sell. JPMorgan ($275, 11-09) and Bernstein ($270, 11-10) raised targets.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The downgrade took ~1.9% premarket on 11-13. The stock closed flat that day (227.46 to 227.73).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced already. The bear case is FY27-28 margins, which the Dec 9 conference resolves, not this print. Two Sells into the print also lower the sentiment bar, which is why this finding is small.

findings.finding: Pro distribution exposure: FBM is ~45% residential (55% commercial) and ADG is fully residential-new-construction exposed. HD cut SRS's organic growth view to low single digits from mid, purely on weak roofing (weak storm season). Weak new construction could push the acquired businesses' Q3 revenue and margin below plan.
findings.link: HD's SRS/GMS are specialty-trade distributors to the same contractor base. GMS (wallboard/ceilings) is the closest analogue to FBM. The roofing weakness HD named is not an FBM/ADG category, so the link is partial.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26: revenue missed ~$150M with the acquisitions inside; stock +2.02%.
findings.why_not_priced: Revenue consensus ($22.36-22.4B, +7.5%) bakes in the acquisitions. A shortfall would show as a revenue miss, as in Q2. Net of the rest: FBM/ADG are roughly 10-12% of sales, while the core comp (the HD read) is the larger driver, so this is sized small.
findings.independence: HD SRS guidance cut (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-home-depot-tops-q3-2026-estimates-shares-slip-93CH-5033430); Stifel's new-construction concern (stocktwits, 2026-11-13).

findings.finding: Macro: Zacks puts existing-home sales at 3.75M SAAR (-8.8% YoY, slowest since 2010) and the 30-year mortgage at an average 7.33% in October. That is a headwind to DIY big-ticket, the line LOW says is under the most pressure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: LOW has printed small positive comps through this housing backdrop for five quarters.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced and public. It is a proxy whose transmission HD's own +2.2% comp partly contradicts (HD grew big-ticket +4.5% through it), so it is sized small. The figures come from an article, not NAR directly.
findings.independence: Ellison: 'most difficult housing market since the financial crisis' (Q1 call, https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/lowe-flags-warning-sign-shoppers-143700930.html).

findings.finding: Hurricane Isaias made landfall as a Category 2 near Destin, FL around 2026-10-09, inside LOW's Q3, with 800k+ customers losing power across FL, AL, GA and the Carolinas. LOW's footprint is overweight in the Southeast. HD, however, described the season as a 'weak storm season' that hurt SRS roofing, and did not cite Isaias as a comp driver.
findings.why_not_priced: A small Southeast storm tailwind late in the quarter. It is weather inference, sized at a fraction, because HD's call (a document) describes the storm season as weak.
findings.independence: HD call transcript describes a weak storm season (partial contradiction), which is why this is sized at +0.1.

findings.finding: Reaction history: in 7 bmo prints since Feb 2025, LOW rose 5 times (median |move| 1.93%). It rose on its last two prints (+2.02%, +4.03%), both of which carried a comp miss or a guide cut alongside an EPS beat. Its one large move (-5.59%, 2026-02-25) came on the first FY guide, which this release does not carry (FY27 is at the 2026-12-09 conference).
findings.why_not_priced: The options imply 3.38% with balanced skew, about 1.75x the median realised. If the market priced LOW's habit of buying in-line-with-guide prints, the skew would lean to calls more than -1.8 vol points. The move history itself comes from the sealed baseline.
findings.independence: The history comes from the sealed baseline (8-K 2.02 acceptance times). It is not independent of the other price findings.

baseline_tension: The options are balanced (skew -1.8, implied 3.38%) and the stock ran ~8 pts ahead of XHB over 20 days before a 5-day giveback. The HD counterparty read is positive and cuts slightly against the run-up, which already prices a better tone, so p_up sits only 3 points above 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar): the EPS bar is sourced to the guide plus three agreeing estimates, but the comp bar is not. The HD counterparty comp finding is capped from +1.0 to +0.8, and p_up moves from 54 to 53.
Lesson 2 (one-offs): the tariff refund is excluded from the guide and models and has only a weak path to the multiple. Cut from +0.4 to +0.25 and kept as one_off.

Lesson 5 (proxies): Placer visits cut from +0.3 to +0.2. The Isaias storm inference is cut from +0.2 to +0.1 because HD's call, a document, calls the storm season weak. The macro housing finding is kept at -0.3 as a small proxy.
Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest): the FBM/ADG new-construction finding is cut from -0.3 to -0.2, because the acquisitions are ~10-12% of sales against the core comp.
Lesson 7: short interest was checked before the negatives (2.0% of float, 3.4 days, not crowded) and the skew is balanced. No change.
Lesson 1: LOW bought its last two in-line or beat prints, while HD's beat was sold today. Both stay as separate findings (+0.3 and -0.4). No change.
